pr_title: fix(resolve): fix resolver not following node resolve algorithm
pr_body:
(fix #2695)

<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

Fixing resolver trying to postfix every file extension to path before trying to resolve to non-posfixed direct match.
Removed the ability to resolve to directory path while not in package.json and index resolution step.
Added 2 tests that previous implementation would fail.

### Additional context

pr_comments: Note: this PR fixes edge cases (included in the tests) and improves performance when the project is using extensions in their imports. Before this PR, for the default config, 7 tryResolveFile would be called before trying for the exact match. With this PR, that 7 tryResolveFile are avoided.

### Describe the bug

Vite's resolver plugin prioritize files with duplicated extensions instead of direct match, inconsistent with node resolve algorithm. 

<!-- If you intend to submit a PR for this issue, tell us in the description. Thanks! -->

### Reproduction
main.js:
```JS
import { file } from './file.js'
console.log(file);
```

file.js:
```JS
export const file = '[success]'
```

file.js.js:
```JS
export const file = '[FAIL]'
```

Result in:
```
>>[FAIL]
```
in production

review_comments: @Timsonrobl is it necessary to remove this branch? Could you add a comment where that branch was explaining why it is not needed in that case?

It is necessary to either remove it or add another parameter and condition `else if (tryDirectory)` otherwise `dont add extension to directory name (./dir-with-ext.js/index.js)` test included in this commit would not pass (and not fail, it would hang test job instead).
I wasn't able to figure out why that branch existed. I checked that it was never reached during `yarn test`, and in my small vue 3 project. Also looking [here](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#esm_resolver_algorithm) I don't understand why resolver would ever need to return directory path. That doesn't mean that reason don't exist 😅
P.S.
Sorry I was talking about `implicit dir/index.js vs explicit file` test that already exist, not `dont add extension to directory name (./dir-with-ext.js/index.js)` from this commit

I just went back in time, and I actually touched this particular line in a commit. You can see how that function was back then here https://github.com/patak-js/vite/blob/844a3820f969f3869295a6c6477085f2899e26ba/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L246

At that point, that was the line that was reached when it wasn't a directory.

Looks like this is the commit where that changed, because `tryIndex` was moved to the dir check: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/commit/c741872e6ca975f507ec89581b742a1da19a0cb0, so when tryIndex is false, if it is a dir, it started to hit that line. Later a check for the case of a file was added at the start of the function, so looks like this is indeed a dead branch due to the evolution of the code. @Timsonrobl you can review this change set if you would like but this PR looks fine to me then.

**thought (dx, readability):** Is this the same as  
```ts
const res: string | undefined = tryResolveFile(file, postfix, options, false, options.tryPrefix)
if (res) return res
```

If so, I think we should write this this way, cause it's much more readable

You mean:
```JS
  let res: string | undefined
  res = tryResolveFile(file, postfix, options, false, options.tryPrefix)
  if (res) return res

  for (const ext of options.extensions || DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS) {
    res = tryResolveFile(
      file + ext,
      postfix,
      options,
      false,
      options.tryPrefix
    )
    if (res) return res
  }
  res = tryResolveFile(file, postfix, options, tryIndex, options.tryPrefix)
  if (res) return res
```
I agree, it looks better. I just tried to touch as little code as possible and maintain original style

Yeah :sweat_smile:, I haven't scrolled down the code so much in the GitHub Web GUI
But yes, please try to improve the code and don't fear touching it :slightly_smiling_face:

It is not bad to refactor code, but let's try to follow Evan's style if there is not a clear gain 👍🏼 
It is easier to check the PRs that way
